candidates.statement: in Scotland, to the Health Facilities Scotland online incident reporting system unless you are a private facility providing care to private clients, in which case you should report to the MHRA and the Care Inspectorate
candidates.context: in England, Wales and Northern Ireland using the Yellow Card scheme in accordance with your organisations medical device policies and procedures. Defective, fake medicines and medical devices, and e-cigarettes

candidates.statement: For established medicines and vaccines you should report all serious suspected ADRs, even if the effect is well recognised.
candidates.context: We are particularly interested in receiving Yellow Card reports of suspected ADRs:

candidates.statement: You should report all suspected ADRs for these products.
candidates.context: New medicines and vaccines that are under additional monitoring have an inverted black triangle symbol (▼) displayed in their package leaflet and summary of product characteristic, together with a short sentence explaining what the triangle means. It does not mean the medicine is unsafe. The MHRA is responsible for maintaining the list of black triangle products in the UK. The European Medicines Agency (EMA) is responsible for maintaining the list of black triangle products in Northern Ireland.

candidates.statement: You should report any adverse incident involving a nicotine e-cigarette or refill container (e-liquid). We work with local trading standards bodies to ensure the safety of these products.
candidates.context: E-cigarettes and e-liquids For more details and a video about what you can report, see What to report to the Yellow Card scheme.

candidates.statement: The e-learning modules should help pharmacists understand how to identify, report and prevent ADRS:
candidates.context: The Centre for Postgraduate Pharmacy Education (CPPE) has developed a series of 3 e-learning programmes with the Wales Centre for Pharmacy Professional Education and the MHRA. The programme has been endorsed by the Drug Safety Research Unit. Adverse drug reactions and medicines safety
